questions.text: एक स्त्री की अंड/डिंबवाहिनी (फैलोपियन नलिका) अवरुद्ध है और उसका आईवीएफ उपचार चल रहा है। जिस तकनीक द्वारा 8 ब्लास्टोमियर से अधिक कोशिकाओं वाले भ्रूण को परिवर्धन हेतु स्थानांतरित किया जाएगा, वह है :
questions.text_english: A female undergoing IVF treatment has blocked fallopian tube. The technique by which the embryo with more than 8 blastomeres will be transferred into the female for further development is:
questions.solution: In Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT), embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred directly into the uterus to complete further development. ZIFT is used for embryos up to 8 blastomeres which are transferred into the fallopian tube.
questions.solution_hindi: आईयूटी (IUT - Intra Uterine Transfer) में 8 ब्लास्टोमियर से अधिक वाले भ्रूण को आगे के परिवर्धन के लिए सीधे गर्भाशय में स्थानांतरित किया जाता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित कथनों में से कौन-सा कथन यथार्थ (सही) है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following statements is correct?

options.A: समयुग्मजी लिंग गुणसूत्र (क्रोमोसोम) (ZZ) पक्षियों में मादा लिंग का निर्धारण करते हैं।
options.B: टिड्डे (ग्रासहोपर) में XO प्रकार के लिंग गुणसूत्र (क्रोमोसोम) नर लिंग का निर्धारण करते हैं।
options.C: मानव में XXY अवस्था टर्नर सिंड्रोम में पाया जाता है।
options.D: समयुग्मजी लिंग गुणसूत्र (क्रोमोसोम) (XX) ड्रोसोफिला में नर का निर्धारण करते हैं।

options_english.A: Homozygous sex chromosomes (ZZ) determine female sex in birds.
options_english.B: XO type of sex chromosomes determine male sex in grasshoppers.
options_english.C: XXY condition in humans is found in Turner's syndrome.
options_english.D: Homozygous sex chromosomes (XX) produce males in Drosophila.

questions.solution: In grasshoppers, the sex determination is of the XX-XO type, where males possess only one X chromosome (XO) and females have a pair of X chromosomes (XX). Option A is incorrect as ZZ produces males in birds; C is incorrect as XXY is Klinefelter's syndrome; D is incorrect as XX produces females in Drosophila.
questions.solution_hindi: टिड्डे (ग्रासहोपर) में लिंग निर्धारण XX-XO प्रकार का होता है, जहाँ नर में केवल एक X गुणसूत्र (XO) होता है। विकल्प A गलत है क्योंकि पक्षियों में ZZ नर बनाता है; C गलत है क्योंकि XXY क्लाइनफेल्टर सिंड्रोम है; D गलत है क्योंकि ड्रोसोफिला में XX मादा बनाता है।

questions.text: उस विकल्प का चयन कीजिए जिसमें 325 लघुबीजाणु मातृ कोशिकाओं के लघुबीजाणुजनन विभाजन के परिणामस्वरूप निर्मित होने वाले परागकणों की सही संख्या को दर्शाया गया है।
questions.text_english: Choose the option that gives the correct number of pollen grains that will be formed after 325 microspore mother cells undergo microsporogenesis.
questions.solution: During microsporogenesis, each microspore mother cell undergoes meiosis to produce four haploid microspores, which develop into four pollen grains. Therefore, 325 microspore mother cells will produce 325 x 4 = 1300 pollen grains.
questions.solution_hindi: लघुबीजाणुजनन के दौरान, प्रत्येक लघुबीजाणु मातृ कोशिका अर्धसूत्री विभाजन द्वारा चार अगुणित लघुबीजाणु बनाती है, जो चार परागकणों में विकसित होते हैं। अतः 325 लघुबीजाणु मातृ कोशिकाएं 325 x 4 = 1300 परागकण उत्पन्न करेंगी।

questions.text: गर्भ की पहली गतिशीलता तथा सिर पर बालों का आविर्भाव सामान्यतः सगर्भता के किस माह में परिलक्षित होते हैं ?
questions.text_english: The first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on its head are usually observed during which month of pregnancy?
questions.solution: The first movements of the foetus and the appearance of hair on the head are characteristic developmental milestones that are usually observed during the fifth month of pregnancy.
questions.solution_hindi: सगर्भता के पाँचवें महीने के दौरान भ्रूण की पहली गतिशीलता और सिर पर बालों का आना आमतौर पर देखा जाता है।

questions.text: बोगेनविलिया के काँटों एवं कुकुरबिटा के प्रतानों (टेंड्रिल्स) के बीच संबंध इसका उदाहरण है :
questions.text_english: Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita are examples of:
questions.solution: Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita are homologous organs. They arise from the same axillary bud position (indicating common anatomical origin) but perform entirely different functions—protection and climbing, respectively.
questions.solution_hindi: बोगेनविलिया के कांटे और कुकुरबिटा के प्रतान समजात अंग (homologous organs) के उदाहरण हैं। वे दोनों ही कक्षीय कली (axillary bud) से उत्पन्न होते हैं, लेकिन उनके कार्य अलग-अलग होते हैं (सुरक्षा और चढ़ने में सहायता)।

questions.text: आंतरिक रक्तस्राव, पेशीय पीड़ा, आंत्र मार्ग का अवरोध तथा अरक्तता जैसे कुछ लक्षण जिसके संक्रमण के कारण उत्पन्न होते हैं, वह है :
questions.text_english: Internal bleeding, muscular pain, blockage of the intestinal passage and anaemia are some of the symptoms caused due to infection by :
questions.solution: Ascaris is an intestinal parasite that causes ascariasis. Symptoms of this disease include internal bleeding, muscular pain, fever, anaemia, and blockage of the intestinal passage due to a massive number of adult worms.
questions.solution_hindi: ऐस्कारिस एक आंत्र परजीवी है जो ऐस्कारिएसिस नामक रोग उत्पन्न करता है। इस रोग के लक्षणों में आंतरिक रक्तस्राव, पेशीय पीड़ा, ज्वर, अरक्तता (एनीमिया) और आंत्र मार्ग का अवरोध शामिल हैं।

questions.text:

(ii) आरएनए पॉलीमरेज II एमआरएनए के पूर्ववर्ती, एचएनआरएनए (hnRNA) का अनुलेखन करता है।
(iii) जब दूत-आरएनए (एमआरएनए) राइबोसोम की बड़ी उपएकक के साथ एकीकृत होता है तब एमआरएनए का स्थानांतरण (रूपांतरण) प्रक्रम प्रारंभ होता है।
(iv) रोध प्रकूट (स्टॉप कोडॉन) में कोई टी-आरएनए नहीं होता है।

questions.text_english:
Choose the correct statements:
(i) Polycistronic mRNA is generally found in eukaryotes.
(ii) The RNA polymerase II transcribes precursor of mRNA, the hnRNA.
(iii) The process of translation of mRNA begins when the mRNA encounters the large subunit of ribosomes.
(iv) Stop codons do not have any tRNAS.
Options:
questions.solution: Statement (i) is incorrect because polycistronic mRNA is found in prokaryotes, while eukaryotes typically have monocistronic mRNA. Statement (iii) is incorrect because translation begins when the mRNA encounters the small subunit of the ribosome. Statements (ii) and (iv) are correct.
questions.solution_hindi: कथन (i) गलत है क्योंकि बहुसिस्ट्रॉनिक एमआरएनए प्रोकैरियोट्स में पाया जाता है। कथन (iii) गलत है क्योंकि एमआरएनए का स्थानांतरण (अनुवादन) तब शुरू होता है जब यह राइबोसोम की छोटी उपइकाई (small subunit) से जुड़ता है। कथन (ii) और (iv) सही हैं।

questions.text: मानव के विलुप्त पूर्वज का नाम बताइए जो केवल फल खाते थे तथा पत्थर के हथियारों से शिकार करते थे।
questions.text_english: Name the extinct ancestor of humans who ate only fruits and hunted with stone weapons.
questions.solution: Australopithecines (Australopithecus) lived in East African grasslands. Evidence suggests they hunted with stone weapons but essentially ate fruits.
questions.solution_hindi: औस्ट्रालोपिथेकस (Australopithecus) पूर्वी अफ्रीकी घास के मैदानों में रहते थे। वे पत्थर के हथियारों से शिकार करते थे, लेकिन मुख्य रूप से फल ही खाते थे।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस रोगजनक/पीड़क के नियंत्रण हेतु बैसिलस थूरिंजिएंसिस का उपयोग किया जाता है ?
questions.text_english: Bacillus thuringiensis is used to control which one of the following pathogens/pests?
questions.solution: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is a soil bacterium that produces protein crystals during a particular phase of their growth. These crystals contain a toxic insecticidal protein that is highly effective in controlling specific insect pests.
questions.solution_hindi: बैसिलस थूरिंजिएंसिस (Bt) एक जीवाणु है जो विकास के दौरान विषैले प्रोटीन क्रिस्टल का उत्पादन करता है। इन प्रोटीनों का उपयोग पीड़क कीटों (जैसे कि कपास के कीड़े, मकई के छेदक) को नियंत्रित करने के लिए किया जाता है।

questions.text: PBR322 में, टेट्रासाइक्लीन, प्रतिरोधी जीन (tetR) में निम्नलिखित प्रतिबंधन एंडोन्यूक्लिऐज में से किसके लिए पहचान स्थल होते हैं ?
questions.text_english: In pBR322, tetracycline, resistance gene (tetr) has recognition site for which of the following restriction endonuclease?
questions.solution: In the cloning vector pBR322, the tetracycline resistance gene (tetR) contains distinct recognition sites for the restriction endonucleases BamH I and Sal I. Cleaving the plasmid at these sites enables insertional inactivation.
questions.solution_hindi: क्लोनिंग संवाहक pBR322 में, टेट्रासाइक्लीन प्रतिरोधी जीन (tetR) के भीतर BamH I और Sal I प्रतिबंधन एंडोन्यूक्लिऐज के लिए पहचान स्थल (recognition sites) मौजूद होते हैं।

questions.text: आरएनएआई में, निम्नलिखित जैवअणुओं में से किसका उपयोग जीनों को निष्क्रिय (शमन) करने में किया जाता है ?
questions.text_english: In RNAi, genes are silenced using which of the following biomolecules ?
questions.solution: RNA interference (RNAi) is a cellular mechanism used for gene silencing in eukaryotes. It involves the use of double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) molecules that bind to and induce the degradation of specific mRNA molecules, thus preventing translation.
questions.solution_hindi: आरएनए व्यतिकरण (RNAi) में जीनों को निष्क्रिय (शमन) करने के लिए द्विरज्जुक आरएनए (dsRNA) का उपयोग किया जाता है। यह विशिष्ट एमआरएनए के साथ जुड़कर इसके स्थानांतरण (अनुवादन) को रोक देता है।

questions.text: पौधों में शाकभक्षियों तथा अपघटकों द्वारा उपभोग के लिए उपलब्ध जैवमात्रा कहलाती है :
questions.text_english: The biomass available in plants for consumption by herbivores and decomposers, is called :
questions.solution: Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the gross primary productivity minus the respiration losses of the plants. It precisely represents the total remaining biomass that is available for consumption by heterotrophs, such as herbivores and decomposers.
questions.solution_hindi: नेट प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (NPP) सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता में से पादपों की श्वसन संबंधी हानियों को घटाकर प्राप्त होती है। यही वह जैवमात्रा है जो शाकाहारियों और अपघटकों के उपभोग के लिए उपलब्ध होती है।

key_points: Site of action for GnRH: Anterior pituitary gland

questions.solution: During spermatogenesis, the hormone Gonadotropin Releasing Hormone (GnRH) acts primarily on the anterior pituitary gland, stimulating it to secrete two essential gonadotropins: LH and FSH. The hormone Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) specifically targets and acts on the Sertoli cells located within the seminiferous tubules. Its main function is to stimulate the Sertoli cells to secrete certain critical factors that heavily assist in the maturation process of spermatids into spermatozoa, a process known as spermiogenesis.

How do 'implants' act as an effective method of contraception in human females?

key_points: Explain mechanism: Implants continuously release progestogens (or combined with estrogen) into the blood, inhibiting ovulation and altering cervical mucus to prevent sperm entry.

questions.solution: Subcutaneous implants act as highly effective contraceptives because they contain progestogens (or a combination of progestogen and estrogen) which are slowly and steadily released into the bloodstream over time. This continuous hormonal release effectively inhibits ovulation and thickens cervical mucus, making it hostile to sperm entry. A major advantage of implants over traditional daily oral contraceptive pills is their long-term efficacy; once inserted under the skin, they provide uninterrupted protection for several years without relying on the user's daily memory and compliance.

questions.text_english: Why and how can bacteria be made 'competent'?

key_points: Explain 'Why': DNA is a hydrophilic molecule and cannot naturally pass through the hydrophobic cell membrane, so cells must be made competent to take up recombinant DNA.
Explain 'How': By treating them with a specific concentration of a divalent cation (e.g., calcium) followed by a heat shock treatment (incubating on ice, then briefly at 42°C, and back on ice).

questions.solution: Bacteria must be deliberately made 'competent' because DNA is a highly hydrophilic molecule that is chemically repelled by the hydrophobic lipid bilayer of the bacterial cell membrane, preventing it from naturally entering the cell. To achieve competence, bacterial cells are chemically treated with a specific concentration of a divalent cation, such as calcium, which vastly increases the efficiency with which DNA enters through pores in the cell wall. Subsequently, the cells undergo a physical heat shock process—they are incubated with recombinant DNA on ice, briefly exposed to a temperature of 42°C, and then quickly plunged back onto ice. This drastic temperature shift forces the bacterium to finally take up the recombinant DNA.
questions.solution_hindi: जीवाणुओं को 'सक्षम' (competent) बनाना इसलिए आवश्यक है क्योंकि डीएनए एक जलरागी (hydrophilic) अणु है जो प्राकृतिक रूप से जलविरागी कोशिका झिल्ली को पार करके अंदर नहीं जा सकता। सक्षम बनाने के लिए, जीवाणु कोशिकाओं को एक विशिष्ट सांद्रता वाले द्विसंयोजक धनायन (जैसे कैल्शियम) के साथ उपचारित किया जाता है। इसके बाद, पुनर्योगज डीएनए (recombinant DNA) के साथ कोशिकाओं को पहले बर्फ पर रखा जाता है, फिर थोड़ी देर के लिए 42°C (हीट शॉक) पर रखा जाता है और अंत में वापस बर्फ पर रख दिया जाता है। इस प्रक्रिया से डीएनए कोशिका के अंदर प्रवेश कर जाता है।

sub_questions.text_english: Biodiversity must be conserved as it plays an important role in many ecosystem services that nature provides. Explain any two ecosystem services.

key_points: Explain pollination: Ecosystems support pollinators like bees and birds which are essential for crop reproduction and fruit production.
Explain oxygen production: Forests (like the Amazon) produce a massive portion of the Earth's oxygen through extensive photosynthesis.

sub_questions.solution: Ecosystem services are the invaluable, life-sustaining benefits that healthy natural ecosystems freely provide to humanity. Two primary examples include pollination and oxygen production. Healthy ecosystems abundantly support diverse pollinators such as bees, bats, and birds, which are absolutely essential for the fertilization of countless agricultural crops, ensuring global food security. Furthermore, vast, biodiverse forests, famously exemplified by the Amazon rainforest, act as massive biological "lungs"; through the process of photosynthesis, they absorb carbon dioxide and release enormous quantities of the breathable oxygen that all aerobic life heavily depends upon.

key_points: State representation: It represents the total mass of living biological material (biomass) present at a particular trophic level at a specific given time.
List measurement 1: Measuring the total number of individuals present in a specific unit area.
List measurement 2: Measuring the total biomass (either fresh weight or dry weight) per unit area.

sub_questions.solution: The 'standing crop' of a given trophic level strictly represents the total, quantifiable mass of living biological material, known as biomass, that is actively present within that specific level at a particular moment in time. Ecologists accurately measure this standing crop using two primary methodologies: they can either meticulously count the absolute number of living individuals present in a defined unit area, or they can calculate the total accumulated biomass per unit area, with measuring dry weight being strongly preferred as it eliminates the massive variability caused by water content.

sub_questions.text_english:
(a) Construct a complete transcription unit with promoter and terminator on the basis of the hypothetical coding strand given below:
ATGCATGCATAG

key_points: Indicate the coding strand with 5' to 3' polarity: 5' - ATGCATGCATAG - 3'
Construct the complementary template strand with 3' to 5' polarity: 3' - TACGTACGTATC - 5'
Label the 5' end of the coding strand as the Promoter site
Label the 3' end of the coding strand as the Terminator site

sub_questions.solution: A complete transcription unit inherently consists of a double-stranded DNA segment defined by strict polarities. By universal convention, the given coding strand runs in the 5' to 3' direction. Therefore, the coding strand is written as 5' - ATGCATGCATAG - 3'. The template strand must be its exact complementary match, running in the antiparallel 3' to 5' direction, which evaluates to 3' - TACGTACGTATC - 5'. Crucially, the functional Promoter region is structurally located at the 5' end of the coding strand (upstream), while the Terminator region is located at the 3' end of the coding strand (downstream).

sub_questions.text: (ख) उपर्युक्त अभिलेखन इकाई से अभिलेखित आरएनए रज्जु की ध्रुवणता दर्शाते हुए अभिचित्रण कीजिए।

key_points: State the RNA sequence: AUGCAUGCAUAG
Indicate the precise RNA polarity: 5' to 3'

sub_questions.solution: During transcription, the newly synthesized RNA strand is built complementarily to the template strand, meaning its sequence matches the coding strand perfectly, except that all Thymine (T) bases are systematically replaced by Uracil (U). Additionally, RNA polymerase only synthesizes RNA in the 5' to 3' direction. Thus, the correctly transcribed RNA strand with strict polarity is 5' - AUGCAUGCAUAG - 3'.

sub_questions.solution: Polyspermy, the dangerous entry of multiple sperms into a single ovum, is effectively avoided through a rapid, biologically programmed membrane block. During fertilization, the very first sperm to successfully penetrate the corona radiata comes into direct physical contact with the zona pellucida layer. This immediate contact triggers complex chemical and structural changes within the zona pellucida, instantly hardening it. This profound modification creates an impenetrable barrier that totally blocks the subsequent entry of any additional sperms, ensuring that only one sperm fertilizes the ovum.

questions.text: अनुकूली विकिरण की परिभाषा लिखिए। डार्विन ने अनुकूली विकिरण की व्याख्या कैसे की ?
questions.text_english: Define adaptive radiation. How did Darwin explain adaptive radiation ?

key_points: Define adaptive radiation: Process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area starting from a point and radiating to other habitats.
Explain Darwin's observations on Galapagos Islands regarding finches.

Detail how Darwin explained that from original seed-eating features, various altered beaks arose, enabling different finches to become insectivorous and vegetarian depending on the specific available ecological niche.

questions.solution: Adaptive radiation is an evolutionary process where different species rapidly evolve from a single common ancestral point within a given geographical area, and subsequently radiate into other distinct habitats or ecological niches to survive. Darwin extensively explained this fascinating phenomenon through his meticulous observations of numerous small black birds, now universally known as Darwin's finches, on the isolated Galapagos Islands. He deduced that all these remarkably diverse finch varieties had evolved on the island itself. From the original basic seed-eating ancestor, immense evolutionary pressure forced the development of various altered beak shapes. These dramatic adaptations enabled the finches to aggressively exploit different new food sources, radiating to become specialized insectivorous and vegetarian finches depending entirely on the specific ecology of their localized habitat.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) How do some viruses cause cancer in humans?

key_points: Explain that cancer-causing viruses are called oncogenic viruses
State that they contain specialized viral oncogenes (v-onc) that can aggressively transform normal host cells into cancerous neoplastic cells upon infection

sub_questions.solution: Certain viruses inherently possess the dangerous ability to cause cancer and are formally termed oncogenic viruses. These viruses contain specialized, highly disruptive genes known as viral oncogenes (v-onc). Upon infecting a normal human cell, these viral oncogenes forcefully disrupt the cell's normal regulatory mechanisms, causing uncontrollable cell division and thereby effectively transforming the normal healthy cell into a cancerous neoplastic cell.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) How do benign tumours turn malignant? How do malignant tumours harm the human body?

key_points: Explain transition: Benign tumours lose their confinement and their neoplastic cells start dividing and growing very rapidly without restraint, invading nearby tissues.
Explain harm: Malignant cells actively starve normal cells by intensely competing for vital nutrients.
Explain harm (Metastasis): Cells slough off from such tumours, enter the blood, lodge in distant organs, and violently start new malignant tumours there.

sub_questions.solution: A benign tumour, which normally remains strictly confined to its original location, turns definitively malignant when its constituent neoplastic cells undergo critical genetic changes allowing them to grow exceptionally rapidly and aggressively invade surrounding healthy tissues. Malignant tumours cause severe harm to the human body in multiple ways. Firstly, because these cells proliferate so rapidly, they voraciously consume massive amounts of oxygen and vital nutrients, thereby literally starving the body's normal cells. Secondly, through a deadly biological property known as metastasis, malignant cells routinely detach from the primary tumour mass, travel extensively through the bloodstream, lodge themselves in distant vital organs, and begin forming entirely new secondary tumours, destroying normal organ function globally.

There are many animals, which have become extinct in the wild, but continue to be maintained in zoological parks.
Answer the questions that follow:

(b) Explain any other two ways which help in this type of conservation.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) What type of bio-diversity conservation is observed in this case ?

key_points: Identify the conservation type clearly as ex situ conservation (off-site conservation)

sub_questions.solution: In this specific scenario where animals are actively taken out of their natural habitats and protected elsewhere, the type of biodiversity conservation being prominently observed is formally called ex situ conservation (or off-site conservation).

sub_questions.text: (ख) ऐसे कोई दो अन्य उपायों की व्याख्या कीजिए जो इस प्रकार के संरक्षण में सहायक हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Explain any other two ways which help in this type of conservation.

key_points: Way 1: Cryopreservation - preserving gametes of threatened species in viable and fertile conditions for long periods using liquid nitrogen.
Way 2: In vitro fertilization or tissue culture - fertilizing eggs in lab settings or propagating plants rapidly using advanced tissue culture methods.
Way 3: Seed banks - storing seeds of different commercially and ecologically important plant strains.

sub_questions.solution: Two highly advanced technological methods that significantly assist in ex situ conservation include Cryopreservation and the use of Seed Banks. Cryopreservation enables scientists to preserve the delicate gametes (sperm and eggs) of highly threatened species in completely viable and fertile conditions for extended periods by storing them in ultra-cold liquid nitrogen. Seed banks serve a similar protective purpose for flora by systematically collecting and safely storing viable seeds of numerous commercially and ecologically important plant genetic strains, safeguarding them from total extinction.

(i) Predation is defined as a fundamental biological interaction where one organism, the predator, actively captures, kills, and feeds upon another organism, the prey. 
(ii) Predation is absolutely necessary in a diverse biological community for two main reasons: Firstly, it functions as the primary conduit for the vital transfer of solar energy fixed by plants upwards through the higher trophic levels. (iii) Predators in nature are described as 'prudent' because evolutionary selection has shaped them not to overexploit their prey. If a predator species became overwhelmingly efficient and entirely wiped out its prey population, the predator itself would subsequently starve and face certain extinction. Therefore, prudent behaviour ensures the long-term survival of both interacting species.

sub_questions.solution: In the E. coli lac operon, the structural genes are efficiently activated by the presence of an inducer, specifically lactose (or allolactose). key_points: Types and location: Alpha-thalassemia is controlled by closely linked genes HBA1 and HBA2 located on chromosome 16. Beta-thalassemia is controlled by a single gene HBB located on chromosome 11.

Cause: It is an autosomal recessive genetic blood disorder caused by a mutation or widespread deletion that entirely results in the severely reduced synthesis of one of the specific globin chains making up hemoglobin.
Symptoms: Severe anemia, pale skin, chronic fatigue, and general physical weakness.

Difference: Thalassemia is fundamentally a quantitative problem (synthesizing too few normal globin molecules), whereas sickle-cell anemia is strictly a qualitative problem (synthesizing a structurally incorrect, malfunctioning mutant globin molecule).

sub_questions.solution: Thalassemia is a serious genetic blood disorder broadly categorized into two types based on the affected globin chain. Alpha-thalassemia is directly controlled by the two closely linked genes HBA1 and HBA2, which are strictly located on chromosome 16. Beta-thalassemia is controlled by a single gene called HBB, which is securely located on chromosome 11. The fundamental cause of this debilitating disease is an autosomal recessive mutation or widespread deletion that completely results in the severely reduced synthesis or total absence of one of the specific globin chains that make up hemoglobin. This significant disruption causes extreme symptoms including severe anemia, pale skin, chronic fatigue, and general physical weakness. Thalassemia differs profoundly from sickle-cell anemia in its core biological mechanism. Thalassemia is fundamentally a quantitative problem because it heavily involves synthesizing too few normal globin molecules, whereas sickle-cell anemia is strictly a qualitative problem, as it involves the synthesis of a structurally incorrect and heavily malfunctioning mutant globin molecule.

key_points: List 4 goals of HGP: To identify all the approximately 20,000-25,000 genes in human DNA, to definitively determine the exact sequences of the 3 billion chemical base pairs, to safely store this massive wealth of information in databases, and to rapidly improve sophisticated data analysis tools.
Methodology 1: Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) - Used by exclusively focusing on actively identifying and sequencing only the genes that are successfully expressed as active RNA.

Methodology 2: Sequence Annotation - Used by blindly sequencing the complete whole genome (encompassing both coding and vast non-coding regions) and later rigorously assigning specific functions to the varying regions.

sub_questions.solution: The Human Genome Project (HGP) was a monumental biological initiative with several highly ambitious goals. Four of its main goals were to successfully identify all the estimated genes present in human DNA, to precisely determine the exact sequences of the 3 billion chemical base pairs that meticulously make up human DNA, to safely store this massive wealth of information in highly accessible public databases, and to rapidly improve the sophisticated bioinformatics tools required for complex data analysis. To achieve this immense feat, scientists heavily relied on two distinctly different methodological approaches. The first method, universally known as Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs), was used by focusing exclusively on identifying and selectively sequencing only those specific genes that are actively expressed as functional messenger RNA. The second method, known as Sequence Annotation, was a much broader, comprehensive approach where researchers blindly sequenced the entire whole genome, encompassing both protein-coding and vast non-coding regions, and subsequently utilized powerful computers to strictly assign specific biological functions to the different sequence regions. In this highly complex sequencing process, YAC, which fully expands to Yeast Artificial Chromosome, was critically used as an advanced, high-capacity cloning vector to safely clone massively large foreign DNA fragments inside engineered host yeast cells, ensuring they replicated flawlessly for subsequent sequencing.

(II) Write the recognition site of this endonuclease restriction enzyme.

key_points: Explain naming convention: The first letter 'E' comes from the genus Escherichia. The next two letters 'co' come from the species coli. 'R' is derived from the name of the bacterial strain RY13. The Roman numeral 'I' indicates that it was the first endonuclease isolated from that specific strain of bacteria.
Write recognition site: 5'-GAATTC-3' on one strand and 3'-CTTAAG-5' on the complementary strand.
Name the overhanging stretches: Sticky ends.

Describe role: They form hydrogen bonds with their complementary sticky counterparts on another DNA fragment, greatly facilitating the action of the enzyme DNA ligase to efficiently join the foreign DNA and vector DNA together to form Recombinant DNA.

sub_questions.solution: EcoR I is named strictly according to universal scientific conventions for restriction endonucleases. The very first capital letter 'E' is directly derived from the genus name of the source bacteria, Escherichia. The subsequent two lowercase letters 'co' are extracted from the species name, coli. The capital letter 'R' specifically designates the particular bacterial strain, which is RY13. Finally, the Roman numeral 'I' clearly indicates that it was the very first active endonuclease enzyme ever isolated from that particular bacterial strain. The highly specific palindromic recognition site for EcoR I is strictly 5'-GAATTC-3' on the coding strand and 3'-CTTAAG-5' on the complementary template strand. When EcoR I cuts the DNA slightly away from the center of this site, it produces distinct overhanging, single-stranded stretches of DNA which are universally named 'sticky ends'. These sticky ends play an indispensable role in the formation of recombinant DNA; because they are complementary, they eagerly form weak hydrogen bonds with corresponding sticky ends created on the vector DNA. This molecular stickiness greatly facilitates the final critical action of the enzyme DNA ligase, which permanently seals the sugar-phosphate backbones, seamlessly joining the foreign DNA and vector DNA together.

(b) (i) Insertional inactivation is a method to detect the recombinant DNA. Explain this method.
(ii) Name the commonly used vector for transferring genes in plants from bacteria.
(iii) How is this able to transform a normal plant cell into a tumour?

key_points: Explain insertional inactivation: A recombinant DNA is inserted within the coding sequence of an enzyme gene (like beta-galactosidase). This insertion physically disrupts and inactivates the gene, meaning the enzyme is no longer produced.

Explain detection: When grown on a chromogenic substrate, non-recombinant bacteria produce the enzyme and form blue colonies, while recombinant bacteria (with the inactivated gene) cannot produce the enzyme and thus form distinct colorless/white colonies.
Name the vector: Agrobacterium tumefaciens (specifically, its modified Ti plasmid).

Explain transformation: The bacterium naturally integrates a piece of its DNA, known as T-DNA, directly into the plant's genomic DNA. This T-DNA forcefully overrides normal cellular controls, compelling the plant cell to divide uncontrollably and form a tumour (crown gall) that continuously synthesizes specialized chemicals required by the pathogen.

sub_questions.solution: Insertional inactivation is an ingenious molecular method used to reliably detect and differentiate recombinant DNA. In this procedure, a piece of foreign recombinant DNA is deliberately inserted directly within the coding sequence of a functional enzyme gene, most commonly the beta-galactosidase gene present on a plasmid vector. This targeted insertion physically disrupts the gene's sequence, effectively 'inactivating' it, meaning the host bacteria can no longer synthesize the active enzyme. For detection, the bacterial colonies are grown on a medium containing a specific chromogenic (color-producing) substrate. Non-recombinant bacteria, which possess the intact gene, produce the active enzyme that reacts with the substrate to form visible blue colonies. In stark contrast, the successful recombinant bacteria fail to produce the enzyme due to insertional inactivation, resulting in distinctly colorless or white colonies, making selection exceptionally easy. For transferring highly desired genes into broadleaf plants from bacteria, the most commonly used biological vector is the heavily modified Ti (tumor-inducing) plasmid extracted from the soil pathogen Agrobacterium tumefaciens. In nature, this remarkable bacterium transforms a normal plant cell into a rampant tumour by naturally integrating a specific segment of its own plasmid DNA, famously known as T-DNA, directly into the host plant's genomic DNA. This inserted T-DNA maliciously hijacks the plant's cellular machinery, forcefully compelling the cell to divide completely uncontrollably, creating a massive tumour (crown gall) that continuously produces specialized nutrients exclusively demanded by the bacterial pathogen.

(a) Study the flow chart given below. Name the hormones involved at each stage and explain their functions.
Hypothalamus -> Pituitary -> Ovary -> Pregnancy

key_points: Hypothalamus secretes GnRH which travels to and strongly stimulates the anterior pituitary gland.
Pituitary secretes powerful gonadotropins (FSH and LH) to stimulate the ovary.
Ovary, functioning under intense FSH/LH influence, develops mature follicles and heavily secretes vital Estrogen and Progesterone.
Progesterone robustly maintains the thick endometrium, completely establishing and flawlessly maintaining the pregnancy.

sub_questions.solution: Based on the provided biological flowchart, the complex hormonal cascade strictly driving pregnancy involves several highly crucial stages. First, the Hypothalamus actively secretes Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH). The primary physiological function of this circulating GnRH is to strongly stimulate the anterior pituitary gland. Second, upon specific stimulation, the Pituitary gland secretes two absolutely key gonadotropins: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and Luteinizing Hormone (LH). FSH actively promotes the healthy growth and rapid maturation of ovarian follicles, while a massive, sudden surge in LH decisively triggers ovulation and ensures the subsequent formation of the active corpus luteum. Third, the Ovary, primarily from the maturing follicles and the newly formed corpus luteum, heavily secretes the vital steroid hormones Estrogen and Progesterone. Finally, Progesterone plays the ultimate critical role bridging the gap to Pregnancy; it profoundly thickens and vascularizes the endometrial lining of the uterus, preventing it from shedding, which is absolutely necessary for the successful, stable implantation of the embryo and the continuous, safe maintenance of the long-term pregnancy.

Differentiate structurally: Perisperm is the persistent, unused diploid remnant of the nucellus tissue; Endosperm is the newly generated, triploid nutritive tissue specifically formed by the primary endosperm nucleus after triple fusion.

sub_questions.solution:
A properly drawn longitudinal section of a maize grain must distinctly and cleanly display the large upper endosperm region completely separated from the lower embryo region. Six crucial structural parts must be clearly labelled: the outermost fused protective layer called the Pericarp/Seed coat, the massive starch-rich bulk Endosperm, the thin proteinaceous outer covering of the endosperm known as the Aleurone layer, the single massive shield-shaped cotyledon termed the Scutellum, the embryonic shoot (Plumule) protected tightly by the Coleoptile, and the embryonic root (Radicle) securely protected by the Coleorhiza. 
Regarding the strict biological differences, Perisperm is fundamentally the persistent, unused remnant of the diploid nucellus tissue that stubbornly remains in some mature seeds, with classic examples being black pepper and beet. Conversely, Endosperm is a newly generated, highly triploid nutritive tissue specifically formed following the triple fusion of the primary endosperm nucleus during double fertilization, primarily serving to deeply nourish the developing embryo; classic prominent examples include maize, castor, and coconut.
